source.original_text: ASTIS generalized analytic ingredient of the symmetry/cosh proof of Zhou–Suzuki Section 6.2 Fact 10, not the full literal-load assertion: for every Borel measurable odd U:R→R and real β with |U(y)|≤β|y| for all real y, every a∈[0,1] and nonnegative variance v, exp(-aU) is integrable under N(0,v), and its integral is at most exp(β²v/2). The source's specific smooth U_i supplies these structural properties in a separate literal-load adapter; its defining parameters, conditional iteration and Lemma6.2 remain outside this ingredient. Exponential integrability is an explicit conclusion elaborating what the source calculation requires.

lean.statement: ∀ {U : ℝ → ℝ} {β a : ℝ} (v : ℝ≥0), Measurable U → Function.Odd U → (∀ y : ℝ, |U y| ≤ β * |y|) → a ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 → MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun y ↦ Real.exp (-a * U y)) (ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 v) ∧ (∫ y, Real.exp (-a * U y) ∂ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 v) ≤ Real.exp (β ^ 2 * (v : ℝ) / 2)

blind_reconstruction.text: For every function U: R -> R, every pair of real numbers beta and a, and every nonnegative real number v, suppose that U is Borel measurable, U(-y) = -U(y) for every real y, |U(y)| <= beta * |y| for every real y, and 0 <= a <= 1. Let gamma_v be the real Gaussian probability measure with mean 0 and variance v; when v = 0 it is the Dirac measure at 0. Then the function y -> exp(-a * U(y)) is integrable with respect to gamma_v, and its real Bochner integral satisfies integral_R exp(-a * U(y)) d gamma_v(y) <= exp(beta^2 * v / 2). Here integrable means almost-everywhere strongly measurable with finite integral of its norm.

import Mathlib.Probability.Distributions.Gaussian.Real
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Trigonometric.DerivHyp

/-!
# Exponential comparison for an odd Gaussian load

The symmetry/cosh argument in Zhou–Suzuki, arXiv:2611.05813v1, Section 6.2,
Fact 10 (source CC BY 4.0), generalized to a measurable odd sublinear load.
This is an original implementation using Mathlib's Gaussian MGF. Integrability
is a conclusion, including zero variance. The paper's literal truncated load
and its conditional level-by-level iteration are separate consumers, not proved
by this generic lemma alone.
-/

open MeasureTheory
open scoped NNReal

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.GaussianOddLoad

/-- A measurable odd load with linear absolute bound has a Gaussian exponential
moment no larger than the corresponding linear load. The absolute bound itself
forces `β ≥ 0`; no positive variance or supplied integrability is required. -/
theorem gaussian_odd_load_bound {U : ℝ → ℝ} {β a : ℝ} (v : ℝ≥0)
    (hU : Measurable U) (hodd : Function.Odd U)
    (hbound : ∀ y, |U y| ≤ β * |y|) (ha : a ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) :
    Integrable (fun y ↦ Real.exp (-a * U y)) (ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 v) ∧
      (∫ y, Real.exp (-a * U y) ∂ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 v) ≤
        Real.exp (β ^ 2 * (v : ℝ) / 2) := by
  let μ := ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 v
  have hβ : 0 ≤ β := by simpa using (abs_nonneg (U 1)).trans (hbound 1)
  have hmag (y : ℝ) : |a * U y| ≤ |β * y| := by
    rw [abs_mul, abs_mul, abs_of_nonneg ha.1, abs_of_nonneg hβ]
    exact (mul_le_of_le_one_left (abs_nonneg _) ha.2).trans (hbound y)
  have hpos : Integrable (fun y ↦ Real.exp (β * y)) μ :=
    ProbabilityTheory.integrable_exp_mul_gaussianReal β
  have hneg : Integrable (fun y ↦ Real.exp (-β * y)) μ :=
    ProbabilityTheory.integrable_exp_mul_gaussianReal (-β)
  have hdom (y : ℝ) : Real.exp |a * U y| ≤ Real.exp (β * y) + Real.exp (-β * y) := by
    apply (Real.exp_le_exp.mpr (hmag y)).trans
    by_cases hy : 0 ≤ β * y
    · rw [abs_of_nonneg hy]
      exact le_add_of_nonneg_right (Real.exp_pos _).le
    · rw [abs_of_neg (lt_of_not_ge hy), neg_mul]
      exact le_add_of_nonneg_left (Real.exp_pos _).le
  have hiPlus : Integrable (fun y ↦ Real.exp (a * U y)) μ :=
    (hpos.add hneg).mono' (by fun_prop) (Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun y ↦ by
      rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_pos (Real.exp_pos _)]
      exact (Real.exp_le_exp.mpr (le_abs_self _)).trans (hdom y))
  have hiMinus : Integrable (fun y ↦ Real.exp (-a * U y)) μ :=
    (hpos.add hneg).mono' (by fun_prop) (Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun y ↦ by
      rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_pos (Real.exp_pos _), neg_mul]
      exact (Real.exp_le_exp.mpr (neg_le_abs _)).trans (hdom y))
  have hsym : (∫ y, Real.exp (a * U y) ∂μ) = ∫ y, Real.exp (-a * U y) ∂μ := by
    have hm : μ.map (fun y ↦ -y) = μ := by
      simp only [μ, ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal_map_neg, neg_zero]
    calc
      _ = ∫ y, Real.exp (a * U y) ∂μ.map (fun y ↦ -y) := by rw [hm]
      _ = ∫ y, Real.exp (a * U (-y)) ∂μ := integral_map (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop)
      _ = _ := by simp only [hodd _, mul_neg, neg_mul]
  have hiCosh : Integrable (fun y ↦ Real.cosh (a * U y)) μ := by
    simpa only [Real.cosh_eq, neg_mul, Pi.add_apply] using (hiPlus.add hiMinus).div_const 2
  have hiLinear : Integrable (fun y ↦ Real.cosh (β * y)) μ := by
    simpa only [Real.cosh_eq, neg_mul, Pi.add_apply] using (hpos.add hneg).div_const 2
  have hcosh : (∫ y, Real.exp (-a * U y) ∂μ) = ∫ y, Real.cosh (a * U y) ∂μ := by
    simp_rw [Real.cosh_eq, ← neg_mul]
    rw [integral_div, integral_add hiPlus hiMinus, hsym]
    ring
  have hmgf (t : ℝ) : (∫ y, Real.exp (t * y) ∂μ) = Real.exp ((v : ℝ) * t ^ 2 / 2) := by
    simpa only [ProbabilityTheory.mgf, zero_mul, zero_add] using
      congrFun (ProbabilityTheory.mgf_fun_id_gaussianReal (μ := 0) (v := v)) t
  refine ⟨hiMinus, ?_⟩
  calc
    _ = ∫ y, Real.cosh (a * U y) ∂μ := hcosh
    _ ≤ ∫ y, Real.cosh (β * y) ∂μ :=
      integral_mono hiCosh hiLinear (fun y ↦ Real.cosh_le_cosh.mpr (hmag y))
    _ = _ := by
      simp_rw [Real.cosh_eq, ← neg_mul]
      rw [integral_div, integral_add hpos hneg, hmgf β, hmgf (-β)]
      rw [neg_sq, mul_comm (v : ℝ) (β ^ 2)]
      ring

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.GaussianOddLoad

lesson.title: An odd sublinear Gaussian load cannot increase the linear exponential bound

sources.label: Zhou–Suzuki, Section 6.2, Fact 10 proof
sources.scope: Generalized symmetry/cosh ingredient; the literal truncated load is a separate adapter and the conditional iteration remains open.

lesson.statement: Let U be a Borel measurable odd real function with absolute value bounded by β times the absolute value of its input. For a gate a between zero and one and a centered Gaussian Y of variance v≥0, the exponential of −aU(Y) is integrable and its expectation is at most exp(β²v/2).
lesson.formula: \begin{gathered}Y\sim\mathcal N(0,v),\quad |U(y)|\le\beta|y|,\quad U(-y)=-U(y),\quad 0\le a\le1,\\ e^{-aU}\in L^1(\mathcal N(0,v)),\qquad \mathbb E e^{-aU(Y)}\le e^{\beta^2v/2}.\end{gathered}
lesson.reader_note: This is the analytic ingredient behind Fact 10, not the construction of the paper's actual U_i or the later conditional-product estimate. Variance zero is included.
assumptions: U: R→R is Borel measurable, and U(−y)=−U(y) for every real y.
β is real and |U(y)|≤β|y| for every y. Evaluating this condition at y=1 forces β≥0; it is not a separate premise.
a∈[0,1] and v is a nonnegative real variance. At v=0 the Gaussian law is the Dirac mass at zero.

steps.title: Establish an integrable envelope first
steps.text: The gate and the load bound give |aU(y)|≤β|y|=|βy|. Each of exp(aU(y)) and exp(−aU(y)) is bounded by exp(|βy|), hence by the sum of two linear Gaussian exponentials. Both envelope terms are integrable by the existing Gaussian MGF theory. Borel measurability of U supplies measurability of the dominated functions.
steps.formula: e^{\pm aU(y)}\le e^{|\beta y|}\le e^{\beta y}+e^{-\beta y},\qquad \int e^{t y}\,\mathcal N(0,v)(dy)=e^{vt^2/2}<\infty.
steps.lean: hβ and hmag derive the signs and absolute bound. hpos/hneg reuse integrable_exp_mul_gaussianReal; Integrable.mono' proves hiPlus and hiMinus. No integrability hypothesis is supplied.

steps.title: Use symmetry to average the two exponential signs
steps.text: A centered Gaussian has the same law after negation, including the Dirac case. Oddness changes U(−Y) into −U(Y), so the two exponential integrals agree. Their average is the hyperbolic cosine integral; the first step justifies splitting the integral of the sum.
steps.lean: gaussianReal_map_neg gives hm. integral_map and hodd give hsym. hiCosh and hcosh use integrable sums, integral_add and integral_div.

steps.title: Compare with the linear Gaussian load
steps.text: Hyperbolic cosine increases with the absolute value of its argument. The pointwise absolute bound therefore compares the nonlinear and linear cosh functions. Both are integrable. Evaluate the two linear exponential integrals at β and −β using the Gaussian MGF; their average is exactly exp(β²v/2), with no lost multiplicative constant.
steps.lean: Real.cosh_le_cosh and integral_mono give the comparison. hmgf reuses mgf_fun_id_gaussianReal. The final arithmetic uses (-β)²=β², preserving the factor 1/2 in the exponent.

lesson.lean_statement: The conclusion is a conjunction: actual Bochner integrability and the exact exponential upper bound. The measure gaussianReal 0 v denotes the real Gaussian with mean zero and variance v, not standard deviation v. hU, hodd and hbound are explicit parameters of the generalized library ingredient.
lesson.lean_proof: One proof constructs the Gaussian exponential envelope, derives integrability, transports the integral by negation, and compares cosh integrals before evaluating the existing MGF. Totalized Bochner integration is never used to evade integrability; it is proved before the moment inequality. No project-owned assumption bundle or unchecked axiom is introduced.
lesson.dependency_notes: All Gaussian law and MGF machinery is reused from pinned Mathlib. Samplinglib owns only this comparison proof; the source-specific truncated function and conditional iteration are planned consumers, not existing Lean calls.
